description: Baseline benchmark setup ran, but product build check failed on missing STDERR_FILENO include in existing src/agent.cpp.

asi.hypothesis: Establish a representative memory operations baseline before optimizing.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks failed because building the full pi-lite target now reports STDERR_FILENO undeclared in src/agent.cpp.
asi.next_action_hint: Add the missing unistd include or otherwise restore product build, then rerun the baseline setup.

description: First passing memory benchmark baseline plus benchmark/check infrastructure and STDERR_FILENO build fix.

asi.hypothesis: Create a stable representative benchmark and fix the product build so future memory optimizations have correctness backpressure.
asi.benchmark_shape: 1000 seeded memories, 96 searches, 48 prompt_context retrievals, 32 steady saves, 32 list calls, 5-trial median.
asi.build_fix: Added <unistd.h> to src/agent.cpp for STDERR_FILENO on POSIX builds.

description: Avoid vector/metadata materialization for list/search and partial-sort top-k; list got faster but search/save worsened overall.

asi.hypothesis: Skipping vector allocation and metadata JSON parsing in list/search would reduce steady-state retrieval latency.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed by ~6.5%; direct BLOB scoring plus per-row category parsing and extra code path made search/prompt/save slower despite list_us dropping from ~210k to ~70k.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the list-specific projection idea separate; for search focus on category parsing, prepared statements, or avoiding repeated full scans rather than BLOB direct scoring as implemented.
asi.phase_learning: list projection is promising, search direct blob scoring is not in this form.

description: Split list into lightweight projection while keeping search full-record scan; list improved but search/save regressed badly.

asi.hypothesis: Use a lightweight SELECT for public list while keeping search semantics with the original full record scan.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed ~20%; duplicating search's SQL path rather than using list likely changed planner/cache behavior and hurt dominant search/save phases, swamping list gains.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not split search/list this way. Try optimizing the existing shared list path in-place, or address save/search scan count with SQL hash exact dedupe before vector near-duplicate scan.
asi.surprise: Even semantically similar full-record search path was much slower than search calling list(), suggesting benchmark is sensitive to extra code/prepare path or noise; confirm with simpler changes.

description: Use partial_sort for top-k memory search instead of fully sorting all scored candidates.

asi.hypothesis: Memory search only returns a small top_k, so partial_sort should reduce dominant ranking cost without changing results or storage semantics.
asi.why_it_worked: Keeps the same candidate scan, scoring, thresholding, and tie-break comparator, but avoids fully ordering discarded tail candidates; improves search, prompt_context, and save near-duplicate phases.
asi.semantic_risk: Low: top-k ordering uses the same comparator as the previous full sort for returned records.

description: Assume normalized embeddings and compute cosine as dot product only; result was slower/noisy versus partial_sort best.

asi.hypothesis: Because HashEmbedder normalizes stored/query vectors, cosine similarity can skip norm and sqrt work and use only dot product.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us was worse than the previous kept partial_sort run (1,710,842 vs 1,690,740); any theoretical arithmetic savings were lost in noise or not dominant versus SQLite/materialization costs.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on reducing rows/materialization/SQL work rather than scalar cosine math; if revisiting, benchmark repeated runs or combine with vector storage changes.
asi.correctness_note: Semantic risk is low for current normalized vectors, but legacy unnormalized DBs would score differently.

description: Reserve memory list result capacity before scanning SQLite rows.

asi.hypothesis: Preallocating the list/search candidate vector to the requested cap avoids repeated vector growth during each memory scan.
asi.why_it_worked: Small allocation reduction in the shared list path used by search, prompt_context, near-duplicate save, and list; primary gain is tiny and likely near noise but directionally consistent for search/prompt/list.

description: Add an in-process MemoryStore record cache and serve list/search scans from it while syncing writes.

asi.hypothesis: Memory operations repeatedly scan the same SQLite rows during a process; caching MemoryRecord rows in MemoryStore and updating the cache on add/update/delete should remove SQLite read/materialization latency without changing persisted storage.
asi.why_it_worked: Dominant search/prompt/list paths now iterate in-memory records instead of preparing SELECTs, reading BLOBs, and reparsing JSON on every call; save near-duplicate checks also reuse the cache.
asi.correctness_guard: SQLite remains source of persistence; add/update/delete still write the DB and log events before updating/removing cached records. Self-test with save/search/update/delete passed.
asi.semantic_risk: Medium: records changed by another process after the cache is loaded are not observed until a new MemoryStore is constructed; acceptable for pi-lite's in-process local-memory UX but worth documenting or adding invalidation later.

description: Use SQLite WAL synchronous=NORMAL for local memory writes and update research notes.

asi.hypothesis: Local memory can safely use WAL with synchronous=NORMAL to reduce fsync/write latency while retaining durable enough behavior for UX memory storage.
asi.why_it_worked: Write-heavy save phases dropped sharply because each memory save writes both the memory row and event log; search/list remained dominated by the in-process cache.
asi.durability_tradeoff: NORMAL in WAL may lose the latest transactions on OS crash/power loss but remains consistent and is a standard performance/durability tradeoff for local caches; not suitable if memory must be fully power-loss durable.
asi.next_action_hint: Further gains should target save's duplicate scan or event write overhead, not SQLite read paths.

description: Add has_similar fast path for save duplicate checks to avoid building search results.

asi.hypothesis: Save only needs to know whether a near-duplicate exists, so it can scan cached records and return a bool instead of calling top-k search and allocating/sorting result records.
asi.why_it_worked: Write-heavy seed/save phases improved by avoiding candidate copies, threshold erase, and ranking work during duplicate checks; search/list behavior for user-facing retrieval is unchanged.
asi.semantic_risk: Low: duplicate check threshold and scope filtering are unchanged; returned duplicate records were never used by save.

description: Search cached records directly and only copy candidates that pass the score threshold.

asi.hypothesis: After adding the in-memory cache, search should not call list() and copy every scanned MemoryRecord before scoring; it can score cache entries in place and copy only threshold-passing candidates.
asi.why_it_worked: Search/prompt phases dropped because below-threshold records are no longer copied with vectors/metadata before ranking; scan caps and category filtering mirror list() semantics.
asi.semantic_risk: Low-medium: preserves the previous 500-candidate effective search cap and 5000 scoped-row category scan cap, but the logic is now duplicated between list and search.

description: Retry dot-product cosine after cache/search optimizations; still slower than normalized cosine baseline.

asi.hypothesis: Once SQLite/materialization overhead is removed, skipping cosine norm and sqrt work might improve cached search/save scans.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus the kept cached direct-search best (72,923 vs 69,066); repeated evidence shows cosine arithmetic is not the limiting factor or dot-only changes optimization behavior unfavorably.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retry dot-only cosine unless vector representation changes substantially; focus on embedding generation, save write overhead, or prompt_context formatting.

description: Avoid token vector and bigram string concatenation in HashEmbedder; benchmark regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Embedding generation allocates token vectors and bigram concatenation strings; streaming token hashing with an equivalent pair hash should reduce query/save embedding overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus cached direct-search best (71,130 vs 69,066), and the change introduced an unused tokenize warning after replacing its only caller.
asi.next_action_hint: Embedding allocation is not a worthwhile standalone target for this workload; if revisiting, remove tokenize and microbench embed equivalence separately before combining with larger changes.

description: Maintain a bounded top-k set during cached search instead of collecting all threshold matches.

asi.hypothesis: Cached search still copies every threshold-passing record and partial-sorts them; maintaining only the best top_k records during the scan should reduce copying and ranking work for retrieval.
asi.why_it_worked: Search and prompt_context phases dropped because only top_k records are copied, while every candidate still gets scored and compared with the same score/updated_at ordering.
asi.semantic_risk: Low-medium: returned top-k should match the previous comparator; tie behavior remains unspecified when score and updated_at are equal.

description: Cache vector norms and reuse each query norm during cached similarity scans.

asi.hypothesis: Preserve true cosine semantics while avoiding recomputing the stored vector norm for every cached search/save comparison by caching vector_norm in MemoryRecord.
asi.why_it_worked: Search, prompt, save, and seed phases improved modestly because each comparison now computes one dot product and divides by precomputed norms; unlike dot-only, this retains compatibility with non-normalized legacy vectors.
asi.semantic_risk: Low: scores remain true cosine; cached norm is populated when loading records and when saving/updating records.
asi.cleanup_needed: The old cosine_similarity wrapper became unused and produced a warning; remove it in a follow-up cleanup experiment.

description: Remove unused cosine_similarity wrapper after norm-cache optimization.

asi.hypothesis: Cleaning up the unused wrapper removes compiler warning/noise and keeps the optimized similarity path focused on precomputed norms.
asi.why_it_worked: No semantic change; benchmark moved slightly faster likely from noise or reduced build/output overhead, and warning output is gone.
asi.semantic_risk: None: no call sites used the wrapper.

description: Reuse memory row timestamp for ADD/UPDATE event logging to avoid extra now_iso8601 calls; regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Save/update call now_iso8601 more than once per persisted memory/event; passing the row timestamp into log_event should reduce timestamp formatting overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (55,728 vs 53,870); timestamp formatting is not a dominant cost and the signature churn did not help.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave log_event API simple; focus on larger write batching or duplicate-scan reductions if optimizing saves further.

description: Bind vector BLOBs directly instead of copying through a temporary string; slight regression.

asi.hypothesis: SQLite bind with SQLITE_TRANSIENT can copy directly from vector data, avoiding the extra vector_to_blob string allocation/copy during add/update saves.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us was slightly worse than best (54,137 vs 53,870); save phase did not improve enough and result is within noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Temporary BLOB copy is not a worthwhile isolated change; if optimizing writes, consider batching or statement reuse instead.

description: Wrap memory row insert and ADD event insert in one explicit transaction; regressed slightly.

asi.hypothesis: Combining the memory INSERT and memory_events INSERT into one explicit transaction should reduce write latency and improve atomicity for save operations.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (55,871 vs 53,870); with WAL+synchronous=NORMAL, explicit BEGIN/COMMIT overhead outweighed any benefit from grouping two inserts.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue per-save explicit transactions. If save write overhead matters, try prepared statement reuse for add/log_event or larger batch APIs, not transaction wrapping.

description: Cache prepared INSERT statements for memory rows and event logs; did not beat current best.

asi.hypothesis: Save still prepares/finalizes INSERT statements for both memories and memory_events every time; caching those sqlite3_stmt handles should reduce write overhead generally.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (54,458 vs 53,870); seed improved but steady total/search noise and added state did not produce a primary improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Prepared add/log_event statement caching is not worth the extra mutable statement lifecycle as an isolated change. Consider reducing cache insertion cost or list copy cost next.

description: Store cache oldest-to-newest and append new records, iterating recent-first for list/search.

asi.hypothesis: upsert_cached_record inserts at the front of a vector on every save after cache load, making saves pay O(n) element shifts; storing cache oldest-to-newest and iterating reverse for recent-first reads should preserve behavior while making new saves append-only.
asi.why_it_worked: Seed and save phases improved because cache updates after each add no longer shift all cached MemoryRecords; list/search still see newest records first via reverse iteration.
asi.semantic_risk: Low-medium: preserves recent-first intent, but equal-second timestamps remain dependent on in-process insertion order similarly to the previous cache behavior.

description: Use float accumulation for cached cosine dot product; save improved but total regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Vectors are float embeddings, so accumulating dot products in float may reduce similarity scan cost enough while preserving practical ranking precision.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (53,940 vs 53,592); save/seed improved slightly but search/prompt got slower and precision semantics are marginally weaker.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep double accumulation for safer cosine semantics. If similarity scan remains a target, explore reducing comparisons rather than lowering arithmetic precision.

description: Reserve extra cache capacity after loading records to reduce add-time reallocations; regressed.

asi.hypothesis: When the cache is loaded and then new memories are saved, vector growth can copy large MemoryRecords; reserving headroom after load should reduce add-time reallocations.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (54,651 vs 53,592); vector growth was not a bottleneck or extra reservation hurt cache locality/noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add fixed cache headroom. Cache append optimization was enough; further save wins likely need reducing duplicate-scan comparisons or persisted write cost.

description: Add slim search_summaries for prompt_context to avoid copying vectors; duplicated search path regressed.

asi.hypothesis: prompt_context only needs memory text/categories, so a slim search path that avoids copying vectors and metadata should reduce pre-model memory injection latency.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed badly (63,901 vs 53,592), especially prompt_us; duplicated search/field-copy code was slower than the optimized shared search path despite copying less vector data.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add a separate summary search path this way. If prompt_context needs optimization, reduce formatting/truncate work or refactor shared top-k code without duplicating candidate assembly.

description: Drop unused scope/hash SQLite indexes now that reads use the in-process cache.

asi.hypothesis: After cached list/search, the scope and hash indexes are no longer used by memory read paths, but every save still pays to maintain them; dropping unused indexes should reduce write latency without changing query behavior.
asi.why_it_worked: Save and seed phases improved substantially because each INSERT updates fewer SQLite indexes. The updated_at index remains for initial cache load ordering, and id lookups still use the primary key.
asi.semantic_risk: Low-medium: current code does not query by scope/hash in SQLite, but dropping indexes could hurt future external/manual SQL queries or future features that search by hash unless they recreate an index.

description: Also drop updated_at SQLite index, leaving memory table unindexed except primary key; primary regressed.

asi.hypothesis: After the cache takes over list/search, even the updated_at index may be unnecessary; dropping it should further reduce insert/index maintenance costs.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (46,814 vs 46,039); seed improved but steady search/prompt/list noise and initial cache ordering cost outweighed write savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the updated_at index. It is still useful for deterministic initial cache load ordering and does not dominate steady save cost after dropping scope/hash indexes.

description: Compute save embedding/vector norm once and reuse it for duplicate check and persisted record; primary regressed slightly.

asi.hypothesis: Memory save embeds the same text once for near-duplicate detection and again for persistence; computing the vector and norm once should reduce save latency without changing dedupe semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (46,201 vs 46,039) despite save_us slightly improving; search/prompt noise outweighed the small save win and signature churn did not justify keeping.
asi.next_action_hint: Embedding reuse may be a tiny save-only improvement but is within noise for total UX metric; focus on bigger retrieval/search or write-index costs.

description: Skip categories_match calls when no category filter is present in cached list/search; retrieval regressed badly.

asi.hypothesis: Most search and prompt_context calls have no category filter, so avoiding categories_match on the hot path should reduce retrieval latency without changing filtering semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus best (72,253 vs 46,039), with search and prompt roughly doubling; the added branch/counter structure likely hurt the optimized no-filter path or caused unfavorable code generation.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not special-case empty category filters this way. Keep the simple categories_match path; future retrieval optimization should reduce similarity comparisons or candidate copies instead.

description: Cache sparse vector entries and use sparse dot products for memory similarity scans.

asi.hypothesis: Hash embeddings are sparse even though stored as 512-float dense vectors; caching non-zero entries per memory and comparing sparse vectors should reduce search and duplicate-check CPU while preserving exact cosine semantics.
asi.why_it_worked: Search, prompt_context, save, and seed phases all improved because similarity scans now merge sparse non-zero indices instead of multiplying all 512 dimensions for every candidate; dense vectors are still persisted for compatibility.
asi.semantic_risk: Low-medium: scores remain true cosine using the same dense values and cached norms, but MemoryRecord copies now include sparse entries and cache memory usage increases modestly.

description: Compute sparse entries and vector norm in one pass; regressed and left vector_norm unused.

asi.hypothesis: After sparse-vector caching, record/query setup still scans dense vectors once for norm and once for sparse entries; combining those into one pass should reduce setup overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary total_us regressed versus sparse-vector best (19,739 vs 18,837), with save/list slower; the combined helper also made the old vector_norm helper unused and produced a warning.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler separate norm/sparse helpers. The main sparse-dot win is already captured; further improvements should avoid adding per-record storage/copy overhead or target SQLite writes.

description: Use dense-query/sparse-record dot products instead of merging two sparse vectors.

asi.hypothesis: Query vectors are already dense in memory, so sparse similarity can iterate only each cached record's non-zero entries and index into the query instead of constructing/merging a query sparse vector.
asi.why_it_worked: Search, prompt_context, save duplicate checks, and seed improved because each comparison became a straight loop over record non-zero entries with fewer branches and no query sparse allocation.
asi.semantic_risk: Low: dot product and cosine normalization are mathematically identical to the previous sparse merge and dense cosine paths for the same stored vectors.
